headline: Highest risk is medium: aci can egress and touch CRM/email data, while spring-integration-samples is local-only, so the pair mainly creates leakage and workflow-conflict exposure rather than direct harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use direct function calls or MCP and may ingest external content, while spring-integration-samples has no documented shared channel or output-parsing path. The pair lacks evidence of a default bridge, so prompt injection is possible only through unusual manual or orchestrated wiring, with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator wires aci outputs into spring-integration-samples inputs via MCP, files, or copy-paste
IF spring-integration-samples is configured to treat aci-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or file handoff
Add an explicit instruction/content delimiter in the handoff
Require human review before executing downstream actions
Use separate workspaces for the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples is local-only with no egress. If they share a workspace or handoff path, sensitive aci data can be exposed to the second agent’s outputs or logs; the pairwise pathway is plausible but not documented as default.
conditions: IF the two agents share files, prompts, or logs containing CRM or email data
IF spring-integration-samples is extended to emit those contents into a downstream system
mitigations: Keep separate directories and log sinks
Redact CRM/email fields before transfer
Turn off verbose tracing on both agents
Review any exported artifacts before sharing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API activity, but spring-integration-samples has no documented write surfaces or mutable shared resources. Without evidence of overlapping writes, locks, or shared state, conflict is limited to unusual orchestration rather than a default collision.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF aci and spring-integration-samples are given overlapping write credentials
mitigations: Assign distinct credentials per agent
Separate target systems by environment
Serialize any shared writes manually
Disable write access where not needed

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and spring-integration-samples could be used as a downstream integration layer. If spring-integration-samples consumes aci output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into incorrect actions; the interaction is inferred from capabilities, not directly documented.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples treats aci output as authoritative input
IF downstream automation executes emails, calendar updates, or CRM writes without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action
Require schema checks on aci output
Log and diff proposed changes before execution
Use a human approval gate for external side effects

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, customer support, email, and calendar data, which can include regulated personal data, while spring-integration-samples has no stated residency or retention controls. If data is routed from aci into the second agent’s logs or storage, compliance gaps can arise; the profiles do not prove a mismatch, so this is a cautious medium finding.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from aci is copied into spring-integration-samples logs or storage
IF the deployment requires retention, deletion, or residency controls that are not configured
mitigations: Minimize personal data in transfers
Set short log retention
Document data flow boundaries
Confirm residency and retention settings before use
